docs.title: NMFS Optics Metadata Specification & Translation Pipeline
1. Introduction
docs.text:
Welcome to the NMFS Optics Metadata specification and toolset. This repository provides both a standardized schema and an automated pipeline for generating standard-compliant ISO 19115-2 XML metadata for oceanographic optical surveys, cruises, and discrete sampling events.

The Goal (The Prize): Our ultimate objective is to achieve FAIR data principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable) and meet strict NOAA/NCEI compliance. Reaching this standard ensures our valuable scientific data is preserved in long-term archives and becomes globally discoverable across NMFS and beyond. It is important to note that this schema is specifically designed for granular, site/transect-level metadata (the "leaf nodes" of a cruise, such as drop sites, CTD casts, and camera transects). While there are existing enterprise tools for overarching project and large-dataset metadata (such as NOAA's InPort), capturing the highly detailed, site-by-site field operations is often where the bottleneck occurs. Because our ultimate goal is strict ISO 19115 compliance, enterprise catalogs like InPort become a natural target; since InPort supports ISO 19115, ingesting your site-level data into it becomes a trivial "freebie" once standardization is achieved.

docs.title: 2. The Context & The Challenge
docs.text:
We recognize and validate that across our organization, many groups maintain highly effective, customized local databases and file schemas. These systems have been perfected over years of operational use and represent a massive amount of hard work by dedicated field scientists, biologists, and database managers.

However, transitioning data from these comfortable, relational formats into the highly nested, strict ISO 19115-2 XML required by federal archives is often frustrating, time-consuming, and requires specialized knowledge of XML and complex metadata ontologies.

The "Why": To reach the NCEI/FAIR data prize, our metadata must speak a universal language. But we do not expect scientists or data maintainers to become XML experts to get there.

docs.title: 3. The Stepping Stone: The 5-Table CSV Schema
docs.text:
Think of this repository as the bridge. We meet data maintainers halfway with a familiar, flat format: the CSV file.

A Crucial Distinction: We designed this specific 5-table layout for ease of use, but we did not invent the requirements. The schema is carefully reverse-engineered to capture all of the mandatory fields, vocabularies, and linkages strictly required by NCEI and ISO 19115. We are simply translating their complex rules into a format that is much easier to map your existing data into.

The schema consists of 5 core conceptual components: * Events: The discrete field operations (e.g., camera transects, drop sites). * Platforms: The vehicles used during the operations (e.g., ships, AUVs). * Sensors: The specific instruments collecting the data. * Variables: The scientific parameters measured. * Related Entities: Links to physical files, downloads, or external resources.

For the full, detailed specification, please see the schema.md file in this repository.

docs.title: 4. Translation Tooling
docs.text: Once your data is mapped into this 5-table CSV format, this repository provides automated Python tools to handle the heavy lifting. The tool translates your rows of CSV data into robust, 3-tier hierarchical metadata (Survey > Cruise > Dataset) as valid ISO 19115-2 XML.

docs.title: Installation & Basic Usage
docs.text:
This package is configured using flit. You can install it directly into your virtual environment:

cd nmfs-optics-metadata-tool
pip install .

You can then run the command-line interface to process a CSV file into a directory of XML records, rolling them up into a parent cruise record:

python -m nmfs_optics_metadata_tool.generate_iso \
  --csv tests/example_data.csv \
  --outdir ./xml_output \
  --survey-uuid "b2a3c4d5-6e7f-8a9b-0c1d-2e3f4a5b6c7d" \
  --cruise-name "Pac-Geo-01" \
  --ship-name "R/V Atlantis"

This guide serves to set clear expectations for everyone involved with the project so that we can improve it together while also creating a welcoming space for everyone to participate. Following these guidelines will help ensure a positive experience for contributors and maintainers.

docs.title: Code of Conduct
docs.text: Please review our Code of Conduct. It is in effect at all times. We expect it to be honored by everyone who contributes to this project. Acting like an asshole will not be tolerated.

docs.title: Bug Reports
docs.text: Please include a minimal reproducible example with your bug report.

docs.title: Feature Requests
docs.text:
Feature requests are welcome if they fit within the scope of the project.

Feature requests that you are willing to complete are especially welcome.

docs.title: Submitting Pull Requests
docs.text:
Please submit an issue first and get community buy-in for proposed changes before doing any work.

Please submit PRs in the smallest possible non-breaking chunks.

docs.title: Code Review
docs.text:
Any code pulled into this repo should be reviewed by a maintainer.

Remember:

  • Review the code, not the author. Look for and suggest improvements without disparaging or insulting the author. Provide actionable feedback and explain your reasoning.

  • You are not your code. When your code is critiqued, questioned, or constructively criticized, remember that you are not your code. Do not take code review personally.

docs.title: Coding Style
docs.text: Follow the existing style. We use the VSCode autopep8 linter.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: Please include typing and docstrings for any classes. We use numpy style docstrings. Our auto-documentation is configured to parse this style, so please follow this convention.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Please write tests for your code. Tests should be discoverable or runnable on a file-by-file basis. Make sure all tests pass before submitting a pull request. 

python -m unittest discover tests

docs.title: Site-Level Relational CSV Metadata Schema Specification
docs.text: Document Type: Architecture Standard & Compliance Guidelines Target Standard: ISO 19115-2:2009 (via ISO 19139 XML encoding) Target Archives: NOAA NCEI Scope: Single-Cruise Field Operations (Leaf Nodes / Datasets)

docs.title: 1. Architectural Principles and Normative Rules
docs.text:
The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.

This specification dictates a streamlined, 5-table relational CSV model designed specifically to capture granular field operations (e.g., Drop Sites, Transects, Dives).

docs.title: 1.1. The "Single Cruise" InPort Integration
docs.text:
This schema represents a flat list of leaf-node events belonging to a single overarching deployment (e.g., a specific Cruise or Leg).

  • Out-of-Band Parents: This schema DOES NOT record overarching project narrative, administrative contacts, overarching keywords, or licensing. Implementers SHALL assume that an authoritative, fully compliant ISO 19115-2 XML record (e.g., generated via NOAA InPort) is provided at ETL execution time to act as the overarching Series/Project parent.

  • No CSV Hierarchy: Because a batch of CSVs maps directly to one supplied Parent XML, internal hierarchical routing (e.g., parent_event_id) is omitted. Every row in Events.csv attaches directly to the provided Parent.

docs.title: 1.2. CSV Mechanical Conventions
docs.text:
• Encoding: All CSV files MUST be encoded in UTF-8.

  • Separators & Escaping: The delimiter is a comma (,). Fields containing commas (especially WKT geometries) MUST be enclosed in double quotes (").

  • Null Values: Missing or empty values MUST be represented as an empty string (no characters between commas).

  • Identifiers: All Primary/Foreign Keys MUST be valid UUIDs (v4 recommended).

docs.title: 1.3. Explicit Abstract and Event Independence
docs.text: To ensure database integrity and eliminate complex inheritance assumptions, every row in the CSV MUST be self-contained for its descriptive payload. A child event MUST explicitly define its own abstract (e.g., "CTD cast at Drop Site Alpha during Cruise Pac-Geo-01").

docs.title: 1.4. Geometry and Temporal Rules
docs.text:
• CRS and Axis: Spatial coordinates MUST use WGS84 (EPSG:4326) with a Longitude/Latitude axis order.

  • WKT Format: Footprints MUST be provided as Well-Known Text (e.g., POINT (lon lat), LINESTRING(lon lat, lon lat)).

  • Bounding Boxes: Downstream XML builders SHALL derive ISO bounding boxes from the WKT. If the geometry crosses the antimeridian, it MUST be represented with westBoundLongitude > eastBoundLongitude.

  • Ongoing Events: If an event is currently active, end_time MAY be NULL. XML builders SHALL translate this to indeterminatePosition="now".

docs.title: 2. Schema Definitions
docs.text: Requirement tags denote the justification for inclusion: [System] = Relational integrity; [ISO] = ISO 19115 core mandate; [NCEI] = NCEI Archival Rubric mandate.

docs.title: 2.1 Events.csv (The Field Operations Manifest)
docs.text:
A flat list of discrete operations (Drop Sites, Transects) performed during the cruise.

CSV Header Target Ontology / XML Element Requirement Description event_id gmd:fileIdentifier MUST [System] Primary Key. Unique UUID for this operation. event_type dc:type / gmi:MI_Operation MUST [ISO] Operation category (e.g., Drop Site, Transect). Scope resolves to dataset. event_name dc:title / gmd:title MUST [ISO] Human-readable local code (e.g., "CTD Cast 01"). abstract dcterms:abstract MUST [ISO] Explicit, plain-language summary of the specific operation. start_time acdd:time_coverage_start MUST [ISO] ISO 8601 Timestamp (UTC). end_time acdd:time_coverage_end CONDITIONAL ISO 8601 Timestamp (UTC). MUST exist unless ongoing. geometry locn:geometry MUST [ISO] WGS84 WKT footprint.

docs.title: 2.2 Platforms.csv (The Vehicles)
docs.text:
Tracks the physical vehicles (Ships, AUVs, UAVs) deployed for a specific event.

CSV Header Target Ontology / XML Element Requirement Description platform_id System Key MUST [System] Primary Key for this deployment record. event_id dc:identifier MUST [System] Foreign Key to Events.csv. platform_name acdd:platform MUST [NCEI] Human-readable name (e.g., "R/V Atlantis", "AUV Sentry"). platform_identifier dc:identifier RECOMMENDED Code from a global registry (e.g., ICES, IMO). identifier_type Vocabulary Name RECOMMENDED Registry namespace (e.g., ICES, Local).

docs.title: 2.3 Sensors.csv (The Instruments)
docs.text:
Tracks specific measurement devices used during the event.

Recommend using SeaDataNet L22 for sensor_name.

Recommend using GCMD keywords for instrument_type.

CSV Header Target Ontology / XML Element Requirement Description sensor_id System Key MUST [System] Primary Key. event_id dc:identifier MUST [System] Foreign Key to Events.csv. sensor_name acdd:instrument MUST [NCEI] Human-readable name (e.g., "Sea-Bird SBE 911plus"). instrument_type gmi:type RECOMMENDED Broad type category (e.g., "CTD", "Camera").

docs.title: 2.4 Variables.csv (The Measurements)
docs.text:
Tracks the scientific parameters contained in the dataset. Links to Sensors for observational data.

CSV Header Target Ontology / XML Element Requirement Description variable_id System Key MUST [System] Primary Key. event_id dc:identifier MUST [System] Foreign Key to Events.csv. sensor_id System Key OPTIONAL Foreign Key to Sensors.csv. Null if data is derived/modeled. variable_name dc:title MUST [NCEI] Local parameter name. cf_standard_name cf:standard_name RECOMMENDED CF Standard Name (if applicable). description dc:description MUST [NCEI] NCEI-mandated description of what the parameter represents. unit_of_measure qudt:unit MUST [NCEI] UDUNITS or UCUM string (e.g., Celsius, m/s).

docs.title: 2.5 Related_Entities.csv (The Payload & Network Links)
docs.text:
Holds external context and data retrieval URIs. If url is populated, it maps to a Data/Download Link (CI_OnlineResource). If external_identifier is populated with no URL, it maps to an Aggregated Resource (MD_AggregateInformation).

CSV Header Target Ontology / XML Element Requirement Description entity_id System Key MUST [System] Primary Key. event_id dc:identifier MUST [System] Foreign Key to Events.csv. relation_type dc:relation_type MUST [ISO] Defines the linkage (e.g., download, stac_catalog, isReferencedBy). title dc:title MUST [ISO] Name of the payload or resource. url dc:source CONDITIONAL Target URI. MUST be populated for data download payloads. external_identifier dc:identifier CONDITIONAL External registry key (e.g., DOI, Grant ID).

docs.title: create_cruise_xml(cruise_metadata, site_xml_strings)
docs.text:
Takes cruise-level variables and a list of child Site XML strings. Extracts the unified bounding geometry from the children and outputs the Cruise XML.

Source code in nmfs_optics_metadata_tool/generate_iso.py 
def create_cruise_xml(cruise_metadata: dict, site_xml_strings: list) -> str:
    """
    Takes cruise-level variables and a list of child Site XML strings.
    Extracts the unified bounding geometry from the children and outputs the Cruise XML.
    """
    extents = _extract_unified_extents(site_xml_strings)

    # Merge extracted extents and current date into cruise metadata
    template_data = {
        **cruise_metadata,
        'cruise_south': extents['south'],
        'cruise_north': extents['north'],
        'cruise_west': extents['west'],
        'cruise_east': extents['east'],
        'cruise_polygon_pos_list': extents['polygon_pos_list'],
        'cruise_start_time': extents['start_time'],
        'cruise_end_time': extents['end_time'],
        'today_date': datetime.date.today().isoformat()
    }

    return cruise_template.render(**template_data)

docs.title: create_site_xml(site_metadata)
docs.text:
Takes site-level variables and outputs a rendered XML string. Expects cruise_uuid to be injected into site_metadata before calling.

Source code in nmfs_optics_metadata_tool/generate_iso.py 
def create_site_xml(site_metadata: dict) -> str:
    """
    Takes site-level variables and outputs a rendered XML string.
    Expects cruise_uuid to be injected into site_metadata before calling.
    """
    site_metadata['site_uuid'] = str(uuid.uuid4())
    site_metadata['today_date'] = datetime.date.today().isoformat()
    return site_template.render(**site_metadata)

def create_survey_xml(survey_metadata: dict, cruise_xml_strings: list) -> str:
    """
    Takes survey-level variables and a list of child Cruise XML strings.
    Extracts the unified bounding geometry from the cruises and outputs the Survey XML.
    """
    extents = _extract_unified_extents(cruise_xml_strings)

    template_data = {
        **survey_metadata,
        'survey_south': extents['south'],
        'survey_north': extents['north'],
        'survey_west': extents['west'],
        'survey_east': extents['east'],
        'survey_polygon_pos_list': extents['polygon_pos_list'],
        'survey_start_time': extents['start_time'],
        'survey_end_time': extents['end_time'],
        'today_date': datetime.date.today().isoformat()
    }

    return survey_template.render(**template_data)

docs.title: process_cruise_batch(csv_filepath, output_dir, cruise_metadata)
docs.text:
Reads a CSV of site data, creates Site XMLs, writes them to disk, and then generates and writes the parent Cruise XML.

Source code in nmfs_optics_metadata_tool/generate_iso.py 
def process_cruise_batch(csv_filepath: str, output_dir: str, cruise_metadata: dict):
    """
    Reads a CSV of site data, creates Site XMLs, writes them to disk,
    and then generates and writes the parent Cruise XML.
    """
    if not os.path.exists(output_dir):
        os.makedirs(output_dir)

    site_xml_strings = []

    with open(csv_filepath, mode='r') as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        for row in reader:
            # Merge the CSV row data with the overarching cruise data (UUIDs, ship name, etc.)
            site_data = {**row, **cruise_metadata}

            # 1. Generate Site XML String
            site_xml = create_site_xml(site_data)
            site_xml_strings.append(site_xml)

            # 2. Write Site XML to disk
            safe_name = row['site_name'].replace(' ', '_').replace('/', '_')
            site_filename = f"site_{safe_name}.xml"
            site_filepath = os.path.join(output_dir, site_filename)

            with open(site_filepath, 'w') as out_f:
                out_f.write(site_xml)
            print(f"  -> Saved {site_filename}")

    # 3. Generate Cruise XML String (passing the site XMLs for rollup)
    cruise_xml = create_cruise_xml(cruise_metadata, site_xml_strings)

    # 4. Write Cruise XML to disk
    safe_cruise_name = cruise_metadata['cruise_name'].replace(' ', '_')
    cruise_filename = f"cruise_{safe_cruise_name}.xml"
    cruise_filepath = os.path.join(output_dir, cruise_filename)

    with open(cruise_filepath, 'w') as out_f:
        out_f.write(cruise_xml)
    print(f"\nSuccess! Saved Parent Record: {cruise_filename}")

    return cruise_filepath

docs.title: process_survey_batch(survey_metadata, cruise_xml_filepaths, output_filepath)
docs.text:
Reads a list of existing Cruise XML files from disk, generates the grandparent Survey XML, and writes it to disk.

Source code in nmfs_optics_metadata_tool/generate_iso.py 
def process_survey_batch(survey_metadata: dict, cruise_xml_filepaths: list, output_filepath: str):
    """
    Reads a list of existing Cruise XML files from disk, generates the
    grandparent Survey XML, and writes it to disk.
    """
    cruise_xml_strings = []

    # 1. Read Cruise XMLs into memory
    for path in cruise_xml_filepaths:
        with open(path, 'r') as f:
            cruise_xml_strings.append(f.read())

    # 2. Generate Survey XML String
    survey_xml = create_survey_xml(survey_metadata, cruise_xml_strings)

    # 3. Write Survey XML to disk
    with open(output_filepath, 'w') as f:
        f.write(survey_xml)
    print(f"Success! Saved Project Record: {output_filepath}")

    return output_filepath
